text:
Elaine: Heads-up: the new pipeline editor has noisy validation. Proposal: keep concise inline errors for field-level mistakes, but switch to a focused typed-confirm modal for destructive actions (delete dataset, reset infra). Open to bikeshedding on copy + a11y. Sam: Inline for live validation is good. For deletes: require typing the exact resource name, e.g. type 'delete analytics-prod'. That blocks accidental taps. Also show the resource path so users know what will be removed. Alex: Accessibility caution: typed-confirm dialogs need proper announcements. Use role="dialog" + aria-modal and announce instructions with aria-live or role="status". Ensure focus lands on the input and keyboard users see a visible outline. Courtney: On error summary: we currently show both inline errors and a top summary all the time. Suggestion: only render summary after a failed submit. Summary should list errors with links that focus the respective input. Avoid duplicating the same text verbatim in both places. morgan: About required indicators we rely on asterisks visually, add explicit helper copy "Required" for screen readers and hide the star via aria-hidden. Example: plus input aria-required="true". Elaine: Example snippet that might work: ```html
Name can't be blank.
``` Pair that with CSS to show the star but keep SRs reading the explicit required state. Sam: Copy for the destructive modal: current "Are you sure?" is weak. Draft: "Delete dataset \"analytics-prod\" — this is permanent and cannot be undone. Type the dataset name to confirm." Primary button text: "Delete dataset" (danger style). Secondary: "Cancel". Show secondary action as plain. Courtney: Also consider a soft-delete alternative: modal+typed-confirm for irreversible deletes, but for user-restorable deletes show a toast with undo and explain retention. Product needs to pick which resource types are soft/hard. morgan: Accessibility nit: don't rely on color alone for danger. Include an icon and a short paragraph describing the impact (e.g., "Removes all runs and logs"). Make sure that description is part of the modal DOM so screen readers announce it. Alex: For summary anchors: clicking an item should move keyboard focus to the field and open any collapsed panels. Use scroll margin + focus() to avoid page jump. Also ensure the summary container has role="status" so SRs are notified when it appears. aria-bot: Checklist: focus trap, role="dialog", aria-modal="true", focus goes to typed-confirm input, visible focus ring, no color-only indicators. Elaine: Action items: 1) Sam to draft modal copy + example mockups, 2) Alex/morgan to prepare aria snippets and asterisk guidance, 3) Courtney to implement summary-on-submit behavior and anchor focus handling, 4) Product (Elaine) to define soft vs hard delete rules. I'll add a Figma mock tonight and drop the link here for review. Sam: I'll post copy drafts in a follow-up message. Elaine: Thanks everyone closing once mock is uploaded.
